HS S O- SH O O Na+ Colouring Agents 1469 Colouring agents have long been used in foods and cosmetics in an attempt to improve the appearance of the product or subject. They are also used in medicinal preparations for several reasons. These include im- proving their acceptability to patients, giving drug for- mulations a distinctive appearance to help identifica- tion and prevent counterfeiting, and increasing the stability of light-sensitive drugs. This chapter describes colouring agents used in medicines and some used in foods, cosmetics, and some medical devices including contact lenses. Most countries restrict the nature and extent of colouring agents used for such purposes. Matters of concern that have received considerable publicity include sensitivity reactions (see Tartrazine, p.1473) and hyperactive behaviour in children (see be- low).
